page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E6.Ax.Flex.16-64 is an x86_64 virtual machine shape utilizing AMD EPYC 9J45 processors operating at a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz. The instance is configured with 16 dedicated physical cores delivering 32 vCPUs through simultaneous multithreading at two threads per core. System memory is sized at 64.0 GB, establishing a 1:2 ratio of vCPU to RAM (2.0 GB per vCPU). Compute cores are fully dedicated, ensuring predictable compute execution without resource contention or burstable throttling.

This instance includes no integrated local NVMe storage and no discrete hardware accelerators, maintaining a GPU count of zero. Persistent file storage and boot environments must be provisioned via external network-attached block volumes. Network connectivity features one complimentary public IPv4 address alongside standard virtual cloud network interfaces.

The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM balance prioritizes raw compute capacity over large in-memory caching. The instance serves multi-threaded, compute-skewed tasks such as parallel compilation, web serving fleets, microservice backends, CI/CD runner pools, and batch processing workloads. Tradeoffs include the requirement for external storage and lower per-core memory density, making memory-bound databases or large analytics engines a less natural fit.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E6.Ax.Flex.16-64 is an x86_64 virtual machine featuring a 2.7 GHz AMD EPYC 9J45 processor configured with 16 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs. Equipped with 64.0 GB of RAM, the instance delivers a compute-oriented 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio offering 2.0 GB per vCPU. The configuration includes no discrete GPU accelerators and provides no local NVMe storage, relying on external network-attached storage volumes for persistent data needs. One complimentary public IPv4 address is included. Operating on dedicated physical hardware slices rather than burstable allocations, this server provides steady processing capacity for parallelized computational tasks, distributed application tiers, CI/CD build environments, and containerized web services that operate efficiently within moderate per-core memory envelopes.
